state.name: Florida
state.agency: Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission
state.peak_intrusion_season: Year-round in Florida's warm climate, with the heaviest raccoon, squirrel, and roof rat attic pressure in the cooler months from November through March, bat maternity season running April 16 through August 14 when exclusion is prohibited, and a post-storm push after summer and fall hurricanes and flooding
state.climate_factor: Florida has no winter off-season for nuisance wildlife — heat, humidity, heavy rain, retention ponds, canals, and year-round breeding for roof rats keep animals active in attics, lanai screens, docks, and yards in every month, and storms regularly displace wildlife into garages, pools, and flooded structures
state.permit_note: Florida does not license nuisance wildlife trappers. Work is done under FWC Rule 68A-9.010 with the property owner's authorization — Florida issues no nuisance-trapper license. Structure rat and mouse work involving chemicals or pesticides is FDACS Chapter 482 pest-control territory; the only related credential is the Section 482.157 Limited Commercial Wildlife Management certificate for nonchemical rodent work in, on, or under a structure, and our crew frames structure rodent work as trapping and exclusion, never chemical control.

Miami-Dade County.region: southeast Florida on Biscayne Bay, bordering the Everglades to the west
Miami-Dade County.nearest_metro: Miami is itself the metro center
Miami-Dade County.habitat_type: dense coastal urban core giving way to western suburbs against Everglades wetlands
Miami-Dade County.regional_wildlife: raccoons, eastern gray squirrels, and roof rats work the homes around Biscayne Bay and Everglades National Park edge, opossums and striped skunks move through yards at night, armadillos dig in lawns and flower beds, and eastern moles tunnel the sandy soils. Green iguanas — a Prohibited species under Chapter 68-5 that can never be relocated or released — bask along canals and seawalls here and are removed humanely on the property, never moved elsewhere, and Burmese pythons are an Everglades-edge concern handled only through Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission programs, not a routine booking
Miami-Dade County.absent_or_rare: gopher tortoises in dry upland ground are State Threatened and left alone — their burrows carry a 25-foot permit buffer and only an FWC Authorized Agent may move one — burrowing owls, sandhill cranes, and wood storks are referral-only, and any alligator four feet or longer that threatens people, pets, or property goes only to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission's Statewide Nuisance Alligator Program, never to a private booking

Suwannee County.absent_or_rare: gopher tortoises in dry upland ground are State Threatened and left alone — their burrows carry a 25-foot permit buffer and only an FWC Authorized Agent may move one — burrowing owls, sandhill cranes, and wood storks are referral-only, and any alligator four feet or longer that threatens people, pets, or property goes only to the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission's Statewide Nuisance Alligator Program, never to a private booking
